contract.title: Compiler proof: executable Jet semantics and complete observation contract
contract.actual: The research defines a conditional preservation claim but does not provide a complete executable formal model of current ratified Jet.
contract.expected: One executable formal semantics covers the ratified language and Jet-owned Core behavior, including acceptance, rejection, effects, failures, resources, and permitted schedules. Its rules are checked against the published language rather than copied from one engine.
steps: Derive the denominator from canonical syntax, typed operations, Core surface and receiver inventories, and applicable target descriptors. Give every construct and boundary an obligation row and live proof owner; unsupported is an open obligation, never an exclusion invented for closure.

Define source states, values, bindings, ownership, stores, tasks, foreign interactions, compile-time behavior, and observable transitions. Include result values, mutations, consumed input, externally visible event order, typed failure, cancellation, termination, and promised progress.

State configuration, arithmetic, scheduling, stack/allocation/fuel, and foreign-contract premises. Preserve defined failures; do not copy CompCert C undefined-behavior refinement into safe Jet. A target-only exhaustion result is allowed only under the existing ratified resource law.

Connect each formal rule to exact current law and executable examples. Reconcile a wrong model against authority; any genuinely unspecified user-visible behavior becomes a named owner gate rather than a silent model choice.

Run the same semantic witnesses and hostile boundary cases through the formal evaluator and the canonical Jet corpus after the compiler baseline is restored. Differences in the specification, model, or implementation receive distinct diagnoses.

Define the Rust, Cranelift, and web-output models needed by the real correspondence arguments. Do not treat a generated mathematical function or foreign-tool model as a verified implementation bridge. Jet-owned unsafe/runtime behavior remains in scope; foreign implementations remain named premises.
criteria: Every current language construct, Core behavior family, and applicable execution boundary appears in the generated obligation relation with a rule and proof owner; omitted or orphaned rows fail the guard.
The executable model distinguishes result, failure, mutation, input consumption, effect order, resource premises, and allowed schedules for the retained nontrivial witnesses.
The model agrees with ratified examples and rejection contracts; a deliberately wrong rule is detected by an independent conformance witness.
No unproved application intention, foreign implementation, scheduler promise, or resource exemption is presented as established Jet semantics.

contract.title: Shared state: atomic snapshots and stale-result rejection
contract.actual: Pool/Id already protects reused resource slots, and Shared/#Transact already owns shared mutation. The proposed delayed-result guard lacks a reusable, fully specified shared-state interface.
contract.expected: A delayed computation can publish only against the same committed state it observed. The chosen interface preserves existing ownership and transactions, rejects ABA and wrong-owner tickets, and never retries effects silently.
steps: Implement only the interface chosen by D-SHARED-REVISION1. Recommended: extend existing Shared<T> with capture() and try_replace(snapshot, value), not a parallel state mechanism.

Capture the value and opaque owner/revision ticket atomically. capture() returns SharedSnapshot<T,T>; capture(pure_projection) returns SharedSnapshot<T,U> and copies only U under existing semantic-copy rules. try_replace accepts the owner-bound ticket and a new T. Tickets grant no mutation right and cannot be fabricated or decoded from ordinary data.

Compare owner and committed revision atomically with publication. A stale ticket returns false without mutation; wrong-owner and exhausted-generation conditions are typed failures. Every committed write advances identity even for A→B→A or equal-value writes. No counter wrap, ticket reuse, or automatic effectful retry is allowed.

Compose with Shared statement writes and #Transact. A successful transaction publishes one committed revision; abort restores value and revision. A snapshot created inside a transaction carries its local write sequence: only a snapshot of the final committed state may become current, and abort invalidates transaction-local tickets.

Use the existing shared lock and lazy revision tracking; do not allocate/copy a second value on ordinary writes when nobody requests snapshots. Reuse the same primitive for compiler/editor delayed publication where its contract applies; Pool/Id retains its separate resource-lifetime law.
criteria: Two competing publications from one snapshot have at most one winner; stale, ABA, wrong-owner, repeated-ticket, and generation-exhaustion cases never overwrite the current value.
Snapshots contain one atomic value/revision pair, preserve ordinary copy and ownership rules, and cannot confer mutation authority or be forged by decoding.
Plain Shared writes and committed/aborted/nested transactions preserve the defined revision law, including snapshots captured before later transaction-local writes.

payload.lesson: A useful explanation shows the rule, its inputs, and whether they still apply. Jet already records facts, proofs, and source changes. This choice decides how those reasons survive for editors, review, and learning without creating another meaning for the program.
payload.story: Maya changes a bound after reviewing an optimization. She wants the old explanation to remain inspectable and the current claim to become stale immediately.

Static derivation, mathematical proof, recorded execution, sampled agreement, and external assumption are distinct evidence methods. A renderer cannot promote one into another. Changed premises invalidate dependents. Stale, expired, redacted, unavailable, unsupported, and budget-exhausted states remain explicit. Hover must not execute user effects.

The same bounds, ownership, failure, mutation, and optimization witnesses must expose the same claim and premises through CLI, editor, review, and learner. Negative controls substitute a source revision, remove a premise, attach a false reason, and mislabel sampled agreement. Every consumer must reject the false current claim.

payload.title: How should Jet reject a result computed from outdated shared state?
payload.gist: How should Jet reject a result computed from outdated shared state?
payload.lesson: A value can change while a task computes its result. Comparing only the value misses a change away and back. Jet already has shared values and transactions. Every choice needs an atomic value-and-revision check, correct ownership, and no silent retry of effects.
payload.story: Maya starts an old search, edits the query, and receives the old result late. That result must not overwrite the current state.
payload.detail:
This is an additive ordinary Core API choice, not new language syntax or a runtime “fact” type. D-CONC-SHARE1, D-SHARED-API1, ownership/copy law, and #Transact remain authoritative. Pool/Id retains its distinct removed-resource generation contract.

Capture value and ticket atomically. Snapshots obey existing semantic-copy eligibility; a pure projection permits copying only an eligible result from a larger value. Tickets are opaque, owner-bound, non-decodable capabilities without mutation authority. A successful replacement consumes no hidden retry and advances the committed revision. Stale returns false without mutation.

Every committed write advances revision, even equal-value writes or a change away and back. Do not wrap or recycle a live ticket’s identity. Wrong owner and exhausted generation produce typed failures. Two publications against one revision have at most one winner. Failed checks do not mutate value or revision.

A transaction publishes one revision on commit; abort restores value and revision. Transaction-local snapshots retain their local write sequence. Only snapshots of the final committed state become current; earlier intermediate snapshots remain stale, and abort invalidates transaction-local tickets. Nested rollback follows the same rule.

Reuse the shared lock and activate revision bookkeeping when snapshots are requested. Ordinary writes must not copy another value merely to maintain a stamp. All applicable modes call one semantic implementation. Negative controls cover concurrent winners, stale/ABA, wrong owner, repeated tickets, exhaustion, and transaction-local snapshots.

The new method is capture, not snapshot. Rollback.snapshot keeps its existing transaction contract and is not repurposed as a publication ticket.

options.name: Checked Shared snapshots
options.detail: Add snapshot and conditional replacement to existing Shared. Existing shared writes automatically invalidate old snapshots. Owner identity and revisions cannot be forged as ordinary data. Projection captures only the data a computation needs. An independent snapshot retains its selected data.
options.technical: Add capture() and capture(project) to Shared<T>. They return SharedSnapshot<T,U>, with an opaque owner/revision ticket and an ordinary owned semantic copy of T or projected U. Projection is pure. try_replace(snapshot, value) returns Bool !SharedRevisionError: false means stale; wrong owner and exhausted generation are typed failures. A ticket grants no mutation right. Existing Shared and transaction laws remain canonical.

options.name: Separate versioned values
options.detail: Add a distinct versioned-value API for conditional publication. The type explicitly advertises versioned publication. Existing Shared need not track revisions. Users choose between two shared-state interfaces.
options.technical: Introduce an ordinary Core Versioned<T> type with replacement-only mutation, snapshot/project, and the same owner/revision/typed-failure law. Shared retains its current interface. Composition between Versioned and Shared transactions must preserve the same atomic publication and rollback rules. No new keyword, sigil, implicit retry, or weaker ownership escape.

options.name: Explicit revision recipe
options.detail: Keep revision management in ordinary Shared transactions. No new public type or method. The protocol uses existing state and transactions. Every writer must maintain the complete revision protocol.
options.technical: Ship the complete canonical recipe and its executable controls, without new API. The full recipe captures value and revision atomically, binds owner identity, advances every committed write, rejects wrap, and composes with transaction rollback. The compact example shows only the late-publication branch. Domain authors remain responsible for applying the protocol at every writer.

comparisons.note: AtomicStampedReference reads and compares a reference and stamp atomically. The caller manages the stamp policy.

recommendation.why: Shared already owns mutation and transactions. Extending it prevents forgotten revision updates without introducing another shared-state mechanism.
gains: Existing shared writes automatically invalidate old snapshots.
Owner identity and revisions cannot be forged as ordinary data.

losses.whyUnavoidable: A delayed computation needs its observed data after the live value changes; projection avoids retaining unrelated fields.

whyNot.reason: A second state type repeats a protocol that can attach to the existing shared value.
A missed writer or owner check silently breaks the stale-result guarantee.

recommendation.tradeoff: Capture only needed fields; preserving an independent past value still requires its data.

payload.title: Where should Jet expose reproducible comparison between two implementations?
payload.gist: Where should Jet expose reproducible comparison between two implementations?
payload.lesson: Running two implementations on the same cases can reveal a difference. Agreement on those cases is not a universal proof. Jet already has corpora, fixtures, and a test runner. Every choice must reject empty or inconclusive runs and preserve the declared comparison rule.
payload.story: Maya replaces a foreign calculation with Jet. She needs reproducible cases, the first difference, and a smaller failing example before accepting the replacement.
payload.detail:
Use D-TESTKIT1, existing test generation, D-RECORD1, and the current runner. No new language annotation, independent runner, external dependency, or generic proof claim. The API remains ordinary Core library surface under the owner’s choice.

Record case/input identity, generator seed when relevant, source/tool/target identity, relation, raw observations, first difference, and a reduced reproducer. Reduction must preserve the mismatch and declared relation. Typed failures, mutation, input consumption, ordered events, and cleanup are observed only when included in that relation.

Matched, mismatch, empty, unsupported, unavailable, timeout, cancellation, and invalid oracle are distinct outcomes. assert_equal() accepts only nonempty valid matched evidence. All-discarded inputs are empty, not matched. Both implementations must consume isolated equivalent inputs and declared environments.

Do not repeat real external effects silently. Effectful scenarios use explicit existing fixtures and reset boundaries. Numeric tolerance or allowed schedule variation requires an explicit relation and appears in the receipt. Equal sampled outputs cannot establish universal equivalence. AOT, run/dev, interpreter, and applicable web routes share the same Core behavior.

options.name: Core Testing comparison
options.detail: Add comparison to the existing Core Testing API. Ordinary tests and foreign adapters share one contract. The result retains replayable differences and explicit outcomes. Existing corpora, fixtures, and reducers remain reusable.
options.technical: Add compare(cases, reference, candidate, relation?) returning a Comparison record with assert_equal(). Default relation is existing typed equality; an explicit relation is part of recorded evidence. Reuse corpus, fixtures, reducer, and test status. Pure functions need no environment setup. Effectful comparisons require explicit isolated recorded scenarios. No implicit external-effect replay.

options.name: Test-runner comparison mode
options.detail: Expose comparison only as a project test command. Projects compare entry points without embedding an API. The existing runner owns replay and failure output. Library tests need process-entry adapters for direct function comparison.
options.technical: Add one ratified CLI mode inside jet test, not another runner. It compares declared project entry points using a case file and explicit observation contract. Preserve the same input isolation, relation, failure, and counterexample rules. Function-level users must provide runnable adapters.
options.code:
# Proposed runner-only interface for the same calculation.
jet test --compare reference.jet candidate.jet --cases cases.json
# Same outcomes, identities, and reduction contract.
# No core.testing.compare API.

options.name: Keep ordinary test loops
options.detail: Use existing corpus tools and explicit assertions only. No new command or library API. Each test states its relation directly. Authors repeat outcome, isolation, and reduction accounting.
options.technical: Keep the existing API and supply a complete canonical testing pattern using corpora, fixtures, and recorded outcomes. Every consumer must explicitly handle empty/discarded cases, unavailable sides, timeout, invalid oracle, isolation, and reduction. No pass-by-vacuity or proof language is permitted.

comparisons.note: Hypothesis supplies generated cases and reduces failures in ordinary tests.

recommendation.why: One library comparison contract serves ordinary tests, foreign replacement, and experiments while reusing the existing runner and evidence.
gains: Ordinary tests and foreign adapters share one contract.

whyNot.reason: It forces direct function comparisons through project-entry adapters.

questions.question: Research Turing Award speeches: what to take, what to avoid, lessons learned.
questions.answer: Transfer the lecture mechanisms with their semantic and engineering premises, not isolated slogans.
questions.acceptance: Implementation-bound proof and falsifiable same-job experiments reject the specific false transfers named in the foundation report.

questions.question: Research postmortems of other programming languages.
questions.answer: Use language postmortems to reject accumulated parallel mechanisms and unearned compatibility obligations.
questions.acceptance: The evaluation names retained-host and ecosystem boundaries; current prerelease truth does not claim historical policy is shipped capability.

questions.question: What should we cherry-pick, and what must be taken with surrounding dependencies to avoid false positives?
questions.answer: Adopt each useful mechanism with its checking, runtime, tooling, and evidence dependencies.
questions.acceptance: A controlled replacement or transformation retains the declared observations and exposes every unproved or foreign assumption.

questions.question: What silhouettes, shadows, and gaps emerge across the research?
questions.answer: Treat lost relationships between claims, routes, identities, and observations as the common missing shape.
questions.acceptance: Missing routes, invalidated premises, and stale publications become counted non-passes rather than disconnected green claims.

questions.question: From first principles, what shapes might Jet be missing?
questions.answer: Deepen the existing semantic, identity, and evidence mechanisms instead of adding fashionable syntax.
questions.acceptance: One authority owns each meaning; views and adapters consume it, and every new public choice is explicit in a ballot.

questions.question: Which cutting-edge computer-science papers could help Jet get ahead?
questions.answer: Turn frontier papers into bounded hypotheses about proofs, effects, staging, temporal identity, and optimization.
questions.acceptance: Each proposed advance has an executable intervention, named premises, falsifier, raw result, and independent replay.

questions.question: Can we create a breakthrough in computer science?
questions.answer: Aim for a useful replicated advance without claiming novelty from a plausible synthesis.
questions.acceptance: The four studies distinguish rejected, supported-with-scope, and unresolved results against named prior work.

questions.question: How can Jet beat other languages to new advances and at fundamentals simultaneously?
questions.answer: Measure new mechanisms and fundamental costs on the same complete jobs in all eight mission areas.
questions.acceptance: Required peers, modes, output/failure, compile/run latency, and memory remain visible per cell; no easier substitute or averaged loss.

questions.question: Aggressive non-cyber red-team audit: where does Jet fall short and have gaps?
questions.answer: Attack false confidence in checking scope, routes, freshness, repair, support claims, and qualification.
questions.acceptance: Wrong-source, missing-mode, discarded-output, invalid-oracle, and stale-candidate controls reject a green result.

questions.question: Which explicit assumptions might be wrong?
questions.answer: Make explicit assumptions executable or label them as assumptions with a precise boundary.
questions.acceptance: Changed or unsupported premises invalidate the claim; agreement, model validity, and implementation correspondence stay distinct.

questions.question: Which implicit assumptions were made and should be reconsidered?
questions.answer: Expose hidden assumptions about identities, shared oracles, scope, and historical evidence.
questions.acceptance: A shared wrong oracle or mismatched historical identity cannot be promoted into current correctness.

questions.question: RLI5 audit of everything across all of Jet.
questions.answer: Derive a complete first-party learner-task denominator and assess explain, predict, modify, and derive separately.
questions.acceptance: Every capability family has tasks or a reasoned non-applicable disposition; simulated friction is not a human study.

questions.question: How do we maximize reasoning about code at every level, in every domain and codebase, including FFI and other languages?
questions.answer: Carry the same reasoning account from expressions through modules, builds, execution, and foreign boundaries.
questions.acceptance: Ordinary tools reveal source identity, ownership/effects, dependency and foreign assumptions, and comparable replacement evidence.

questions.question: How does Jet become a readable, comprehensible, learnable next-generation development experience rather than just a language?
questions.answer: Make source, verdict, execution, explanation, repair, and recheck one deterministic development experience.
questions.acceptance: The same facts and actions work through CLI and ordinary editor without AI or mandatory Studio.

questions.question: What creative solutions can improve teachability?
questions.answer: Teach through prediction, a valid counterexample, one controlled change, and unfamiliar transfer.
questions.acceptance: A copied solution or canned explanation cannot satisfy all learning tasks; unknown and unavailable remain honest.

questions.question: How can a newcomer learn programming principles, not merely Jet?
questions.answer: Teach programming principles through structurally different tasks, not only Jet syntax repair.
questions.acceptance: Learners must derive the same principle in a different program; real transfer claims require real participant evidence.

questions.question: What visuals or LSP features can teach concepts and features and show relationships?
questions.answer: Project values, ownership, state, effects, dependencies, and counterexamples from source-bound records.
questions.acceptance: Keyboard/text/no-color/reduced-motion and narrow/wide paths preserve complete evidence across current, stale, and unavailable states.

questions.question: Where are friction, rough edges, and other shortfalls?
questions.answer: Put the shortest sound path on frequent work and keep rare expert controls discoverable and auditable.
questions.acceptance: First-hour and recurring reasoning tasks record concrete failure, repair, latency, and understanding limits rather than an invented usage survey.

questions.question: How do we ensure foundations, features, tooling, syntax, core libraries, and APIs are fully functional and work as intended?
questions.answer: Join every advertised capability to its intended contract, actual route, consumed oracle, and candidate.
questions.acceptance: Every applicable row is counted; a declaration, test name, missing mode, or discarded result cannot count as functional evidence.

questions.question: How do we ensure no missing or broken functionality ever and verifiably correct behavior always, to build trust?
questions.answer: Replace an impossible unconditional guarantee with complete conditional proof and independent qualification obligations.
questions.acceptance: All Jet-controlled stages need bound checked arguments; model, foreign, resource, and application-intent boundaries remain explicit.

questions.question: Can we aggressively research and test theoretical compiler optimizations?
questions.answer: Test theoretical optimizations under exact machine semantics before measuring whole-job profit.
questions.acceptance: Five experiment families reject illegal rewrites and legal slow plans separately, preserving failure, input, identity, and order.

questions.question: How do we obtain an effective, efficient test suite rather than a bloated one?
questions.answer: Keep distinct behavioral detection and mandatory obligations, then minimize redundant cost.
questions.acceptance: Every removal has replacement evidence; unique historical/seeded detectors and required modes survive measured selection.

questions.question: How do other languages test and establish correctness?
questions.answer: Use proof, conformance, differential generation, regressions, platform fleets, and workloads for their different claims.
questions.acceptance: Each evidence class retains its scope and candidate identity; no one class silently substitutes for another.

questions.question: What do their test harnesses look like?
questions.answer: Make corpus, oracle, raw result, reducer, identity, and invalid outcomes first-class in existing harnesses.
questions.acceptance: Replay rejects stale inputs, wrong artifacts, zero-valid runs, invalid oracle contracts, and harness failure reported as success.

questions.question: What about their CI/CD pipelines?
questions.answer: Qualify one candidate through existing CI rather than assemble unrelated green fragments.
questions.acceptance: Source/tool/model/checker/artifact changes invalidate dependent claims while historical receipts and ratified thresholds remain intact.

questions.question: How can Jet prevent common software glitches, bugs, and errors at language level so adoption raises overall software quality?
questions.answer: Prevent modeled defect classes at the earliest sound layer and name the remaining domain assumptions.
questions.acceptance: Ownership, stale publication, foreign lifecycle, and declared comparison controls reject the modeled bug without claiming all domain intent.

questions.question: If a game were written in Jet instead of C++, which common glitches should become impossible or less frequent?
questions.answer: Separate memory/lifetime safety, entity identity, scheduling, clocks, capacity, and game rules.
questions.acceptance: Real game witnesses test stale/reused identity, time and overload rules, callbacks, and replay; bounded JavaScript models are not Jet proof.

questions.question: What is our trade space, and where can its bounds be pushed?
questions.answer: Design away representational and interface tradeoffs before accepting physical or informational limits.
questions.acceptance: Each remaining ballot loss has a concrete reason; safety, expert control, performance cells, and complete behavior are not traded away.

questions.question: How creatively can language shape, code generation, and optimization address ordinary bugs and errors?
questions.answer: Use existing types/facts, shared lowering, explicit state identity, and evidence-backed tools to prevent repeated mistakes.
questions.acceptance: The fix closes the defect shape across applicable modes and consumers instead of adding a spelling-specific special case.

questions.question: How do we get to stable release through a clear plan rather than minutiae?
questions.answer: Deliver foundations and complete evidence first, then one frozen candidate under the existing sustained handoff and owner gate.
questions.acceptance: No stale green, missing required proof, averaged loss, synthetic handoff evidence, automatic self-hosting gate, or false 1.0 claim can qualify.

interviewRequirements.requirement: Beginner magic, full expert control, enterprise auditability; friction tracks frequency; effort is not a rejection reason.
Proof remains valuable alongside tests; evaluate self-hosting before gating.
Near-native common-language work, C/C++ adoption, reviewable foreign conversion.
No AI dependency or optional AI mode in the proposed experience.
Prerelease breaking changes allowed; no current Jet-version migration support; preserve external contracts after 1.0.
Fresh Astra authorship; factual Luna collection; Main orchestration; permitted challenge and HTML mechanics only.
Reports, useful retained demonstrators, deduplicated cards, decisions, verified linked HTML; no production fixes.
Dedicated report section covering new features, APIs, surfaces, syntax, architecture, tools, ideas, and concepts, with related concrete cards and owner ballots.
